gloss: to fit into, to set into; to frame

definitions.gloss: to fit into, to set into, to embed
definitions.explanation: To insert or place something precisely into a space or frame designed for it.

definitions.gloss: to frame, to entrap, to set up
definitions.explanation: To trick someone into a disadvantageous situation, often by deception or manipulation.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}にガラスを{嵌|は}め{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To fit glass into a window frame.

examples.japanese: {指輪|ゆびわ}に{宝石|ほうせき}を{嵌|は}め{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: A gemstone was set into the ring.

examples.japanese: パズルのピースを{嵌|は}め{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To fit a puzzle piece into place.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{詐欺師|さぎし}に{嵌|は}め{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: He was set up by a con artist.

examples.japanese: {罠|わな}に{嵌|は}め{込|こ}まれたことに{気|き}づかなかった。
examples.english: I didn't realize I had been set up.

examples.japanese: {証拠|しょうこ}を{捏造|ねつぞう}して{彼|かれ}を{嵌|は}め{込|こ}もうとした。
examples.english: They fabricated evidence and tried to frame him.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB: {嵌|は}める (to fit, to insert) + {込|こ}む (to go into) = to fit firmly into place

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive. Takes を to mark what is being fitted in, and に to mark where it's being fitted.

KANJI NOTE: {嵌|は}める can also be written in hiragana as はめる in everyday use. The kanji {嵌|はま} is not commonly known.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{宝石|ほうせき}を{嵌|は}め{込|こ}む (to set a gemstone)
・ガラスを{嵌|は}め{込|こ}む (to fit glass into a frame)
・{罠|わな}に{嵌|は}め{込|こ}む (to entrap)
・{嵌|は}め{込|こ}まれる (to be framed - passive)

SENSE 2 NUANCE: The figurative meaning of "framing" or "trapping" someone is colloquial and often used when discussing schemes or fraud. The passive form {嵌|は}め{込|こ}まれる is common for victims of such schemes.

RELATED ～{込|こ}む COMPOUND VERBS:
・{追|お}い{込|こ}む - to corner
・{誘|さそ}い{込|こ}む - to lure into
・{押|お}し{込|こ}む - to push into
